label: GPON OLT class C++, 16 ports
notes: Class C++, the 35 dB reach-extended G-PON class, per ITU-T G.984.2 (08/2019) Appendix V reach-extended tables and ITU-T G.9805 (02/2022) Tables 6-1 and 6-2, which tabulate the same 20..35 dB ODN as class D: OLT receiver minimum sensitivity -35 dBm, minimum overload -15 dBm, OLT mean launched power +6..+10 dBm. Two corrections on 2026-11-24. The receiver carried -33/-8, which matched neither the standard nor any vendor module and left the class unreachable upstream: an ONU launching +0.5 dBm into a -33 dBm receiver has 33.5 dB against a 35 dB class, so the class verdict passed while the headroom verdict failed on the same row. At -35 the pair is 35.5 dB and the class is the tighter verdict again. The launch moved from +5..+9 to the standard's +6..+10; launch is the one figure that genuinely varies by module - ZTE's 033030400016 C++ SFP prints +3..+7 dBm with the same -35/-15 receiver - so a bought module may sit outside this row's range, and a budget's outside-range warning is the correct answer to that, while the receiver figures and the 35 dB class do not move. The overload is the trap with no reach answer: at a +6..+10 dBm launch against a -15 dBm overload point an ODN shorter than roughly 21-25 dB overdrives the far end, and a bare patch into an ONT will blind it - the budget's attenuator verdict names the pad to fit, and G.9805's 20 dB class D floor is the shortest ODN the class allows. Downstream the deepest ONTs in this catalogue are the C+ receivers at -30 dBm (gpon-ont-c-plus-1ge, gpon-ont-4ge), which still cover the class: 6 + 30 = 36 dB against 35. Ports 16 is a line-card size, not a standards figure. Replace with the OLT's own datasheet for the line card actually purchased before construction.
